review.verdict: EXISTING_REASONING_CORROBORATED; no class promotion by this reviewer
review.receipt_reasoning: Loads normalized interval noncancelled orders then buckets Cairo wall-clock hour; returns24fixed buckets. DST repeated hours merge and skipped hour gets0, intentional display decision requiring documented test. Cash collection may differ from order net.

source_evidence.behavior: For single-day range, chooses `LoadHourlySeriesAsync`; other date ranges use daily buckets. Returns granularity label with a 24-point series.

Uses BusinessDateRange.ToUtcRange; loads noncancelled orders created in [start,end), selecting CreatedAtUtc, TotalPiastres and cumulative RefundAmountPiastres. Converts timestamp to Cairo timezone, groups on wall-clock Hour (0..23), sums Total-Refund and order count, then emits exactly 24 labeled buckets and fills absent hours with zero.
Defines business date as Cairo local date and converts Cairo-midnight boundaries into UTC. Single-day hourly query thereby uses that business-day interval.
Range method delegates to `UtcRangeForBusinessDates`, which normalizes reversed endpoints; the hourly series caller is single-day only through LoadTrendAsync.
Hourly series is part of trend DTO; headline comparisons use shared sales/expense report methods. Trend is a read aggregation, no write.
Series conveys label, NetSalesPiastres and OrderCount; it has no payment-channel or refund-event timestamp field.
Integration test asserts 24 hour points and that point net sums to cash headline NetSalesPiastres after one cash sale. Static test evidence only; not run.

review.substantive_assessment: The source confirms the receipt’s key claims: a one-business-day chart uses Cairo wall-clock hour, not UTC hour; cancelled orders are excluded; each bucket contains order count and order-level net after cumulative refunds; zero-activity hours remain visible. Its use of order creation time means refunds remain attached to the original sale hour rather than the hour processed, consistent with an order-date net-sales chart, but not equivalent to refund-date cash activity. It is a read-only aggregation and does not change financial state.
counterevidence_and_limits: The integration test explicitly validates 24 points and reconciliation of point totals to the dashboard sales headline for a forward single-day case.
BusinessClock defines Cairo business-date windows, and shared SalesReport uses the same order created-at interval and canceled-state exclusion.

No explicit DST test found. The implementation intentionally emits 24 wall-clock labels; if Cairo’s offset transition produces a 23- or 25-hour UTC interval, any repeated local hour is combined and an absent hour remains a zero bucket. Whether this is desired visualization semantics needs a product/report contract; static sources do not establish deployment dates or actual visual outcome.

No test in reviewed dashboard class covers mixed payment types, refunds processed at a different time from sale, cancelled orders in hourly buckets, or DST boundary. No runtime/provider behavior verified.
remaining_actions: Add integration coverage with orders on multiple Cairo hours, a cancelled order, and a refund to establish expected bucket net and counts.

Confirm the report contract uses order-creation-hour net sales; if the user needs refund processing-hour activity, expose a distinct series based on refund event timestamps rather than changing this net sales series silently.
Decide whether 24 wall-clock labels with DST repeated/missing hours is the intended business display, and add timezone transition tests if relevant.
No correctness fix or finding is recommended from static review absent changed reporting requirements.
